cells.tense: The fire is lit now and you have the pen in your hand.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Take something your people already do together. Imagine this week what it could become, then make the first move toward that, even if the move is telling a single person about it.
cells.core:
You keep a shared thing alive — a practice, a weekly gathering, a way your people do things — and you do it with warmth rather than force. The room can feel the fire is tended. What makes it work is that direction comes from feeling, not from a plan you're defending. You move when you're genuinely engaged, and people follow that kind of movement without being asked to.

What this balance is free to feed next is imagination. Not a grand vision — a fresh look at something you already keep going. Dream the next step and take it. The step is small and real: a sentence to somebody, a change to how the thing is done. What you'll have is a practice that's alive rather than merely maintained. You'll know because the people in it will start bringing things to it themselves.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the fire warm, and it runs on feeling, not force.
cells.verb: tending the fire of a shared thing so it keeps going
cells.place: where meaning is handed down between people, in rituals and practices that carry what has proven worth keeping

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future that cannot be written in yet.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: While you're pushing a shared plan or tradition forward, pause and say only the part the other person can take in right now. Save the rest for later.
cells.core:
You hold a shared thing — a tradition, a team's way of working, a family's rhythm — and lately you're pushing it toward a future you can already see. The push has outrun the room. People around the shared thing get the whole plan at once, and some of them nod while they've stopped following. The drive is real and it's yours. What's missing is the pause that lets other people arrive.

What restores the current is tuning what lands against what can't. Say the true part that can be heard and hold the rest back for a moment it fits. Aim for direction that comes from real engagement rather than the timetable in your head. The shared thing doesn't need pulling forward. It needs walking with.
cells.sheetLine: You're pulling the shared thing forward faster than it can arrive.
cells.verb: tending the fire of a shared thing so it keeps going

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you some time back.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Take a shared practice that has quietly finished. Tell whoever needs to hear it that it's done, and carry forward the single piece of it still worth keeping.
cells.core:
Where meaning gets handed down between people, the attention has gone quiet. Something that used to be kept — a ritual, a shared way of doing things, a regular gathering — is still on the calendar and nobody is near it. You're part of it and not quite in it. The fire isn't out. Nobody has been to it. Direction that used to come from genuine engagement has gone still.

Don't push feeling back into the starved spot. Do the structural thing instead: release what is done and keep what serves. Tell whoever needs to hear it that it's finished, and take the one piece worth carrying. Letting a finished thing finish is what makes room for the next. What you'll have is a shorter list of what you actually keep, and a fire with something to burn.
cells.sheetLine: Something shared has quietly finished, and you haven't said so.
cells.verb: tending the fire of a shared thing so it keeps going
cells.place: where meaning is handed down between people, in rituals and practices that carry what has proven worth keeping

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Name a shared thing that needs to change, then change one concrete piece of it this week and finish that piece before you go back to anything else.
cells.core:
You already carry a shared thing further than you let on. You keep a tradition, or a group's way of doing things, quietly going, and your account of yourself is that you're in it like the rest. The people inside it read it differently. They've watched something shift since you came in, and you haven't claimed any of it.

What brings the current back is the earliest version of the move: breakthrough by steady effort. Name one shared thing that needs to change, change one concrete piece of it, and finish that piece this week. Don't announce a plan. Just do the inch. What you'll have is a structure that's genuinely different, and a claim on it you can stand behind without performing anything.
cells.sheetLine: You've already changed the shared thing, and you won't say so.
cells.verb: tending the fire of a shared thing so it keeps going
cells.place: where meaning is handed down between people, in rituals and practices that carry what has proven worth keeping
